title: Chanakya
copyrightReason: Original 2021 composition by Rishab Rikhiram Sharma (released 15 Aug 2021 on Des Records); the composer is living.
raga: Not officially named; the notes match Asavari thaat with shuddha Re (D natural minor / Aeolian), close to Raag Jaunpuri
structure: Starts slow with a free, alaap-like sitar intro over a D drone. Then a short, repeating minor-key hook comes in over the groove. It builds with longer runs and call-and-response between the sitar and the rhythm, and ends with fast, tightly picked phrases on the higher strings.
notes: Chordify and song-metadata listings agree on D minor and 143 BPM. Chordify lists Dm as the main chord. Gm, C and A# (Bb) fit the scale as passing chords, but no source confirmed them. Melody is copyrighted, so no transcription is stored. The duration was not verified (0 = unknown). The structure text is a general description and should be checked against the recording.

title: The Burning Ghat
copyrightReason: Original composition released 4 Jul 2025 (single, Platoon); the composer is living.
strummingPattern: Slow down-strums on the beat, or let a drone ring under the melody
structure: A slow, meditative tribute to the eternal pyre at Manikarnika Ghat in Varanasi. Sitar carries the melody over an ambient bed of electronic synths and piano, with tabla and percussion. It moves from a contemplative opening to a fuller, rhythmic middle and returns to calm near the end. Runs about 7 minutes.
notes: Confirmed: release date 4 Jul 2025, length 6:58, tabla by Prashant Trivedi, piano by Shaan Chhadva, percussion by Rakesh Bhardwaj, theme of Manikarnika Ghat. No source online (Chordify, Tunebat, press) gives the key, BPM or raga, so tonic, key, scale, bpm and chordVamp are left empty. Find these by ear or with a key/BPM analyser before the app uses this entry for chord or note detection.

title: Shiv Kailash (Shiv Kailashon Ke Vasi)
copyrightReason: This sitar arrangement and recording (Live in Mumbai, Sitar for Mental Health tour) are copyrighted. The underlying 'Shiv Kailashon Ke Vasi' is a traditional Himachali folk bhajan.
structure: A folk-bhajan melody for Shiva, played on sitar with the crowd singing along. A short, simple tune repeats with more ornaments each time. It starts gently and builds into a rousing, clap-along rhythm by the end.
techniqueFocus: simple major-key melody on one string
playing along with a three-chord strum
notes: Chordify gives key D with chords D, G, A, and 97-103 BPM depending on the live version (100 used here). A folk-bhajan chord site gives G, C, D, Bm in 7/4 (a 7-beat cycle like Rupak taal) for the generic bhajan in a different key. The folk tune is traditional and could later become its own public-domain entry, but this entry covers only Rishab's arrangement, so no melody is stored. The year is approximate (the Live in Mumbai release).

title: Tandavam
copyrightReason: Original composition and recording released 25 Feb 2022 (the Shiva stotram text it uses is traditional, but the music is new).
structure: A high-energy Shiva piece that mixes sitar, a chanted Shiva stotram and electronic drums. Sitar hooks alternate with chanted sections and grow into a powerful, dance-like climax.
notes: Released 25 Feb 2022. Key/BPM are from one aggregator only (D major, 125 BPM; Shazam shows 62, the half-time reading). Not double-checked, and the major vs Mixolydian scale is not confirmed. Only the tonic D chord is listed until checked by ear. Has chanted vocals, so it is not strictly an instrumental.

title: Doordarshan Signature Tune
artist: Pt. Ravi Shankar & Ustad Ali Ahmed Hussain Khan
copyrightReason: Composed 1976 by Ravi Shankar (died 2012) with Ali Ahmed Hussain Khan; still in copyright and tied to Prasar Bharati.
structure: A short sitar-and-shehnai theme, about half a minute, that played as Doordarshan's on-air logo animated. Ravi Shankar built it as a variation on his tune for 'Saare Jahan Se Achha'. One flowing phrase rises and settles back home.
techniqueFocus: short melodic phrase on one string
notes: First broadcast 1 Apr 1976. A favourite single-string piece for Indian beginners. Not a recent trending fusion piece, but it fits the 'sitar melody' theme. No source found for key/BPM, so those are left empty; check by ear. Do not store a melody transcription. Can be swapped for a newer fusion piece (e.g. an Anoushka Shankar track) if wanted.

title: Jana Gana Mana
copyrightReason: Words and music by Rabindranath Tagore (died 1941); Indian copyright expired at the end of 2001 (60 years after death).
strummingPattern: D - D - (slow, stately; or just single notes)
structure: One stanza (the official 52-second version): long repeated-note phrases on Ga, a climb to Pa for the Punjab-Sindh line, phrases that keep resolving to Sa, and the rising 'Jaya he' ending that finishes on Ma.

sargam.name: Jana gana mana adhinayaka jaya he
Jana gana mangala dayaka jaya he
Jaya he, jaya he, jaya he

techniqueFocus: small range (lower Ni to upper Sa)
notes: Checked line by line against harmoniumweb.org and synthesizernotes.com, which agree on the notes (only the lyric alignment differs). Note values are approximate, since the sources give no rhythm. Chords are simple suggestions, not an official harmony. In-app copy should ask for respectful practice (e.g. stand for full performances); the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act 1971 penalises disrespect, not playing it.

title: Raghupati Raghav Raja Ram (Ram Dhun)
artist: Traditional (popularised by V. D. Paluskar / Gandhi)
copyrightReason: Text traditionally attributed to Lakshmanacharya (17th c.); the well-known tune is linked to Vishnu Digambar Paluskar (died 1931), so any copyright ended long ago.
raga: Mishra Kafi / Mishra Khamaj flavour (uses both Ga and komal ga, both Ni and komal ni)
strummingPattern: D DU D DU (bhajan keherwa feel)
structure: Call-and-response Ram dhun. A refrain starts on lower Pa and settles on Sa, an answering line dips into komal Ga and komal Ni, and a middle line ('Ishwar Allah tero naam') rises to Ma and returns to the refrain.
techniqueFocus: lower-octave notes (Pa, Dha, Ni below Sa)
notes: Checked against hitxp.com (Western notes in C, credits Paluskar), notesandsargam.com and notationsworld.com. The opening (.P S S S, then a dip to .N/.D) and the 'Patit pavan' line (R g R S .n .D) agree. Sources differ on whether the first lower Ni is komal, and on the exact cadence of 'Sita Ram'; the majority natural-Ni reading is used. Other tunes exist (e.g. the Kuch Kuch Hota Hai film version, which is copyrighted). Chords are suggestions.

title: Vaishnav Jan To Tene Kahiye
copyrightReason: Text by Narsinh Mehta (15th c.); sung to a traditional tune in Mishra Khamaj; no living author.
raga: Mishra Khamaj (major scale plus komal Ni on the way down)
strummingPattern: D - DU - UDU (slow keherwa / dadra feel)
structure: Every verse uses the same four-line tune. Line 1 sits around Ga and Ma, lines 2 and 4 climb through Pa and Dha to upper Sa and come back down through komal Ni, and line 3 hovers on Dha and komal Ni before the cadence back to Sa.

sargam.name: Vaishnav jan to tene kahiye je

notes: Checked against bansurisargam.blogspot.com and notesandsargam.com. Both have the same contour, including komal Ni in lines 2-4. Note values are approximate. Original recordings are often in C#; Sa = C is used here for easy fingering.

title: Om Jai Jagdish Hare
copyrightReason: Written by Shardha Ram Phillauri (died 1881); the aarti tune is traditional. The 1970 film version (Purab Aur Paschim) is a separate copyrighted recording.
strummingPattern: D - D U D U (slow 6/8 aarti sway)
structure: Refrain plus verses that share one tune. The refrain sits on Sa and rises to Pa and Dha on 'Swami jai Jagdish hare'. The middle lines wave around Re, Ga and Ma, and each verse ends by falling to lower Ni and Dha before the refrain comes back.

sargam.name: Bhakt janon ke sankat / Daas janon ke sankat

notes: Checked against harmoniumguru.in, harmonium.indianraag.com, synthesizernotes.com and notesandsargam.com. All agree on the refrain, the 'Bhakt janon' line and the 'Kshan mein door kare' cadence. The rest of each verse ('Sukh sampati ghar aave / Kasht mite tan ka') reuses the 'Bhakt janon' / 'Kshan mein' tunes. Note values are approximate.

title: Jai Ganesh Jai Ganesh Deva
copyrightReason: Traditional aarti, text attributed to Surdas (16th c.); traditional tune. Commercial recordings (e.g. Anuradha Paudwal, T-Series) are copyrighted, but the tune itself is not.
raga: Major scale with a passing tivra Ma (F#) in the antara
structure: The refrain 'Jai Ganesh' climbs Sa-Re-Ga and repeats Ga. The 'Mata jaki Parvati' line dips to lower Ni and resolves to Sa. The antara ('Ek dant dayavant') jumps up to Pa and swings between Pa and tivra Ma before coming down to Ga.

sargam.name: Antara: Ek dant dayavant, char bhuja dhari
Antara: Mathe sindoor sohe, moose ki savari

techniqueFocus: tivra Ma vs shuddha Ma (F# vs F)
notes: Checked against harmoniumguru.in and synthesizernotes.com, which agree on the refrain, the dip to lower Ni and the antara contour. The tivra-Ma swing in 'char bhuja dhari' comes from harmoniumguru (marked M') plus a search snippet saying the original scale is F# with a vikrit swar of tivra Ma. synthesizernotes' plain-text copy did not show its tivra markings. Note values are approximate.
